chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from al-Nadr, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Abu Basir,
who said: I asked Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him): 'At what [distance] does a man shorten [his prayer]?' He said: 'At the whiteness of a day (bayadh yawm), or two barid.'

key_terms.بَرِيدَيْنِ: two barid — unit of distance (one barid = 4 farsakhs ≈ 22 km); two barid ≈ 44 km, the canonical minimum masafa in Shia fiqh
key_terms.بَيَاضِ يَوْمٍ: whiteness of a day — colloquial Arabic expression for the distance traversable in one day's travel, equivalent to two barid
key_terms.يُقَصِّرُ: shortens (prayer) — performs qasr al-salat, the two-rak'a shortened prayer obligatory for travelers

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance (masafa) that obligates shortening of prayer (qasr al-salat) according to Imam al-Sadiq in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Abu Basir asked Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) about the minimum travel distance that obligates shortening of prayer (qasr al-salat). The Imam answered with two equivalent expressions: 'bayadh yawm' (the daylight/whiteness of a day — the distance visibly traversable in a single day's journey) and two barid (a postal-route unit of distance, each barid being four farsakhs, totalling approximately 44 km). This is a foundational legal ruling for the traveler's prayer in Shia jurisprudence, and the figure of two barid (eight farsakhs) became the canonical minimum masafa (travel distance) for qasr.
